issues.detail: The Hebrew 'קִדַּמְתִּי בַנֶּשֶׁף' means 'I anticipated/prevented the twilight' (i.e., I rose before dawn), but the Chinese '我夜間起來' (I rose at night) omits the specific sense of 'anticipating/preventing' and the precise time 'twilight/evening' (נֶשֶׁף), replacing it with a general 'night'.

The Hebrew 'וָאֲשַׁוֵּעָה' means 'and I cried out/pleaded' (from שׁוע, to cry for help), but the Chinese '為你話語焦渴' (I thirst for your words) changes the action from crying out to thirsting, which is not in the Hebrew.
The Hebrew 'יִחָֽלְתִּי' means 'I hoped/waited' (from יחל), but the Chinese omits this verb entirely, leaving only the thirst metaphor.
